text: I really enjoy being right and then it turns out in the working world, that did not serve me so great.
speaker: Ami Vora
context: Lenny shares a quote from Boz (Meta's CTO) about Ami's ability to respond with curiosity when faced with profound disagreements. Ami explains that her natural tendency to always be right didn't work well in professional settings. She had to learn to prioritize getting to the best outcome rather than being the person who's always right, which required setting aside her ego and being open to learning from others' perspectives.
text_ko: 저는 제가 맞는 걸 정말 좋아했어요. 그런데 막상 직장 생활에서는 그게 별로 도움이 되지 않더라고요.
text_zh: 我特别喜欢证明自己是对的，结果到了职场上发现，这样做对我一点好处都没有。
text_es: Me encanta tener la razón, pero resulta que en el mundo laboral eso no me sirvió para nada.
key_sentence: that did not serve me so great.
original_text: I really enjoy being right and then it turns out in the working world, that did not serve me so great. I think the hard part is sublimating your ego a little bit and saying it's more important to get to the outcome than to be right.

text: If we all agree that the feeling of something should be, I'm sitting in Dolores Park with my friends on a sunny Saturday, then people will just naturally build something that feels more consistent.
speaker: Ami Vora
context: Ami is discussing how to use metaphors and imagery to rally teams around a shared vision. She explains that when teams agree on a specific feeling or metaphor for their product - in this case, the relaxed, friendly atmosphere of hanging out with friends in a San Francisco park - it guides design and product decisions naturally without needing detailed specifications for every choice.
text_ko: 모두가 어떤 느낌이 있어야 한다고 동의한다면, 나는 친구들과 함께 화창한 토요일에 돌로레스 파크에 앉아 있을 거예요. 그러면 사람들은 자연스럽게 더 일관된 느낌을 주는 뭔가를 만들게 될 거예요.
text_zh: 如果我们都认同某种感觉应该是这样的，比如在阳光明媚的星期六，我和朋友们坐在多洛雷斯公园，那么人们自然会创造出更一致的东西。
text_es: Si todos estamos de acuerdo en que la sensación de algo debería ser, como estar sentado en el Parque Dolores con mis amigos en un sábado soleado, entonces las personas naturalmente crearán algo que se sienta más coherente.
key_sentence: People will just naturally build something that feels consistent when they agree on feelings.

vocabulary.definition: Consistent means acting or done in the same way over time, ensuring reliability and uniformity in performance or behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, consistency is vital for brand reputation, customer experience, and operational efficiency, as it builds trust and predictability among stakeholders.
vocabulary.nuance: While often viewed positively, overemphasis on consistency can stifle innovation; thus, it should be balanced with flexibility when necessary.

text: For me, the hill climb is all about the difference between a local optimum and a global optimum.
speaker: Ami Vora
context: Lenny asks Ami about her hill climb metaphor. Ami explains this metaphor represents the challenge of leaving a good situation (local optimum) to pursue something much better (global optimum). The hill climb describes the difficult decision of giving up current success to cross an uncertain valley and climb a higher mountain, with the understanding that remembering the potential reward helps sustain you through the difficult transition period.
text_ko: 제게 힐 클라임(hill climb)은 지역 최적(local optimum)과 전역 최적(global optimum)의 차이가 핵심이에요.
text_zh: 在我看来，爬山算法(hill climb)的核心就是局部最优和全局最优的区别。
text_es: Para mí, esto de ir subiendo la cuesta (hill climb) tiene que ver con la diferencia entre encontrar lo mejor a corto plazo versus encontrar realmente la mejor solución global.
key_sentence: The hill climb illustrates the difference between local optimum and global optimum.
original_text: For me, the hill climb is all about the difference between a local optimum and a global optimum. You're standing on top of the hill, you're looking down, you can see rolling hills, the sheep, the grass, whatever, but then, way off in the distance you can see a mountain. And the thing that gets me through the valley is remembering what the summit feels like.

vocabulary.definition: The most favorable condition or level for achieving the best possible outcome. In various contexts, it refers to the ideal point where efficiency or effectiveness is maximized.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, 'optimum' often refers to the best allocation of resources or strategies that yield the highest return on investment or performance.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'optimum' suggests the best possible scenario, it can imply that there are multiple acceptable levels, and it is often used in contrast to 'suboptimal'.

text: I think the hard part is just sublimating your ego a little bit and saying it's more important to get to the outcome than to be right.
speaker: Ami Vora
context: Lenny asks Ami for practical advice on how to disagree skillfully and respond with curiosity like Boz described. Ami explains that the core challenge is managing your ego and prioritizing collective success over personal validation. She emphasizes that personal growth fundamentally involves internal struggles, and the desire to be right is one of the most difficult impulses to overcome because it's tied to our natural self-protective instincts.
text_ko: 힘든 건 자존심을 조금 접고, 내가 옳다는 걸 증명하기보다 결과를 내는 걸 더 중요하게 여기는 거예요.
text_zh: 我觉得最难的就是要放下面子，承认达成目标比证明自己对更重要。
text_es: Creo que lo difícil es bajar un poco el ego y decir que es más importante llegar al resultado que tener razón.
key_sentence: it's more important to get to the outcome than to be right.
original_text: I think the hard part is just sublimating your ego a little bit and saying it's more important to get to the outcome than to be right. And I think all of growth is a battle with yourself, but this is one of the hardest ones because we all want to be right, we all want to protect ourselves.

vocabulary.definition: The result or effect of an action, decision, or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management and strategic planning, understanding the desired outcomes is crucial for measuring success and aligning team efforts.
vocabulary.nuance: While often used interchangeably with 'result,' 'outcome' can imply a broader scope, including both intended and unintended consequences.

text: I think we misuse product reviews sometimes as ways to get decisions and actually, they should be ways to calibrate on principles. So what you don't want is to come to a product review for every single that you want to make.
speaker: Ami Vora
context: Lenny asks Ami for additional advice about running effective product reviews beyond keeping them simple and having recommendations. Ami explains that product reviews are often used incorrectly as decision-making forums when they should actually be used to establish consistent principles. Instead of seeking approval for every individual decision, teams should use reviews to align on decision-making frameworks that enable autonomous choices in the future.
text_ko: 가끔 제품 리뷰를 결정을 내리는 수단으로 잘못 활용하는 경우가 있는 것 같아요. 사실 제품 리뷰는 원칙을 조율하는 방법이어야 해요. 그래서 매번 모든 결정에 대해 제품 리뷰를 하러 가는 건 피해야 해요.
text_zh: 我认为我们有时错误地使用产品评审作为决策的依据，实际上它们应该是用来校准原则的工具。因此，我们不希望每次做决策时都依赖于产品评审。
text_es: Creo que a veces hacemos un mal uso de las revisiones de productos como una forma de tomar decisiones, cuando en realidad deberían servir para calibrar principios. Lo que no queremos es acudir a una revisión de producto por cada decisión que queremos tomar.
key_sentence: We misuse product reviews instead of using them to calibrate on principles.

vocabulary.definition: To adjust or fine-tune something to ensure accuracy or optimal performance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, calibrating often refers to aligning strategies, metrics, or processes to ensure they meet established standards or objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'calibrate' implies precision and adjustment, it is often used in contexts where ongoing evaluation and refinement are necessary.

vocabulary.definition: Fundamental truths or propositions that serve as the foundation for a system of belief or behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, principles guide decision-making, corporate culture, and ethical practices, helping organizations maintain consistency and integrity.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'principles' often carries a moral or ethical weight, suggesting a commitment to core values rather than just operational guidelines.

vocabulary.definition: Choices made after consideration, often involving a selection between alternatives.
vocabulary.businessContext: Decisions in business can range from strategic planning to daily operational choices, impacting the direction and success of an organization.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'decisions' can imply a level of finality and responsibility, often associated with the consequences that follow the choice made.

text: I think execution eats strategy for breakfast and that's something we used to say a lot at Meta. It was just the most important part and I was well-trained in that.
speaker: Ami Vora
context: Lenny brings up Ami's belief that execution beats strategy every time, asking her to elaborate on this philosophy. Ami explains this was a core lesson from Meta, emphasizing that while strategy is intellectually engaging and allows for big-picture thinking, customers only experience the actual product in their hands. She argues that focusing too much on abstract strategic planning can distract from solving real customer problems today.
text_ko: 저는 실행이 전략을 압도한다고 생각해요. 'Execution eats strategy for breakfast'라는 말을 메타(Meta)에서 정말 자주 했어요. 실행이 가장 중요한 부분이었고, 저는 그걸 잘 해내도록 훈련받았어요.
text_zh: 我觉得执行力比战略重要多了，这是我们在Meta经常说的一句话。执行力是最关键的，我在这方面训练得很扎实。
text_es: Creo que la ejecución se come a la estrategia en el desayuno y eso era algo que decíamos mucho en Meta. Era simplemente lo más importante y me entrenaron muy bien en eso.
key_sentence: Execution eats strategy for breakfast; strategy is just pie in the sky stuff.
original_text: I think execution eats strategy for breakfast and that's something we used to say a lot at Meta. It was just the most important part and I was well-trained in that. That was one of the key lessons that I learned there, and it's because when you have... Look, strategy is super fun. You get to think about all this pie in the sky stuff.

vocabulary.definition: The act of carrying out or putting into effect a plan, order, or course of action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, execution refers to the implementation of strategies and plans to achieve desired outcomes, often emphasizing the importance of timely and effective action.
vocabulary.nuance: While execution implies the practical application of ideas, it can also suggest a focus on results over theoretical planning, making it a critical term in performance-driven environments.

vocabulary.definition: A high-level plan designed to achieve specific goals or objectives, often involving the allocation of resources.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business and startups, strategy encompasses the long-term vision and direction of the organization, guiding decision-making and resource allocation.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a deliberate and calculated approach, distinguishing it from more spontaneous or reactive methods of operation.
